A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOBODY. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material that was relocated or split.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo gravity/friction experiments and component ablations, with normalized scores and variability across three seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds kinematic/morphology shifts, Adroit manipulation evaluations, dynamics-learning comparisons, sensitivity results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, cycle loss, rollouts and Q-weighted policy objective match. However, v2 explicitly adds a target-domain encoder-loss formula and changes DARA classifier labels and inputs in Appendix C.1 inconsistently with its domain-classification description. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences represent procedural changes, clarified omissions or transcription errors.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates four MuJoCo locomotion tasks under gravity/friction shifts. v2 retains these and adds 32 medium/hard kinematic and morphology settings on those tasks, plus eight Adroit Pen and Door settings. Tables 4–5 substantially broaden physical conditions and task requirements.

E2.justification: The five benchmark baselines—BOSA, IQL, TD3-BC, MOPO and DARA—and the CQL ablation remain. Section 4.4/Table 3 adds a dedicated dynamics-learning comparison using target-only, combined-data and source-pretrain/target-finetune models. Combined-data and fine-tuning comparators are newly evaluated within this controlled comparison.

E3.justification: v2 Table 9 changes MOBODY/TD3-BC BC-weight candidates from {0.1, 1, 10} to {0.05, 0.1, 1}, and MOBODY/MOPO uncertainty penalties from 5 to {1, 5, 10}. New dynamics comparisons introduce rollout MSE evaluated using policies at four training checkpoints and controls sharing the base architecture. Original dataset sizes and score normalization remain; revised settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The original A1–A4 ablations, including Hopper results, are retained unchanged. v2 adds direct dynamics-error and training-strategy analysis in Table 3, joint BC-weight/uncertainty-penalty sensitivity analysis in Table 7, and computational-cost comparisons in Table 8. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond component removal.

E5.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation tables still report means and standard deviations over three seeds. However, v2 drops v1 Appendix A.3's explicit three-seed replication statement for every hyperparameter configuration, and new Tables 3–5 and 7 do not clearly specify their replication counts. This changes reporting completeness without establishing any change in actual run counts.

E6.justification: Table 1 and every original ablation entry are numerically unchanged after matching relocated tables. v2 adds results for 40 new settings, with MOBODY attaining the highest mean in 26/32 locomotion and 6/8 Adroit cases, plus dynamics-error, sensitivity and timing results. Table 3 does not show uniformly lower MOBODY error: Walker2d-gravity-0.5 MSE is 1.93 versus 1.87 for combined-data training.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's factorization/likelihood argument and revises domain-specific loss expressions. Appendix C.1 corrects the DARA reward-adjustment sign to agree with v1's Algorithm 2, but introduces non-equivalent classifier equations assigning target labels to source examples and including the next state in the state-action classifier. These are limited mathematical revisions and errors; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central model-based off-dynamics RL and target-Q-weighted behavior-cloning contributions remain. v2 broadens the headline empirical claims to MuJoCo and Adroit and alternative dynamics learners, retaining the 58% gravity/friction claim while adding a 25% kinematic/morphology claim.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations involving low-shift training regions, shared structure and domain-specific actions, limitations of pretraining/fine-tuning, and prevention of representation collapse. It also interprets sensitivity and computational costs. Conversely, v1's explicit limitation concerning domains without shared state representations and transitions, and its safety-oriented impact discussion, are removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds joint-range and limb/finger-size modification instructions, practical hyperparameter recommendations and runtime estimates. It removes the explicit best-configuration selection description, D4RL source-data attribution and MOPO capacity-matching rationale. Hardware, network dimensions and the code repository address are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the distributionally robust MDP research strand and its foundational, online and offline RL citations, together with the Jin et al. and Zhan et al. references supporting earlier theoretical motivation. Positioning concentrates more on learned target dynamics versus filtering, reward regularization and generic transfer. Much of the remaining related work is relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and dynamics-learning explanation are extensively rewritten. Related work and algorithm/reward/uncertainty details move to appendices, the experimental narrative is reorganized, and the limitation and impact sections disappear. This constitutes substantial rewriting and structural revision beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel summary figure and tables for dynamics comparisons, additional benchmarks, sensitivity and runtime. The original gravity/friction plot becomes appendix Figure 4; original Table 2 is split into Walker2d Table 2 and Hopper Table 6. Results tables are relocated near the document's end, while the architecture figure is retained.

improvement.justification: The added physical-shift and manipulation evaluations and direct dynamics-learning comparisons provide stronger support for MOBODY's applicability and design choices; sensitivity and runtime measurements also improve practical assessment. These benefits are partly offset by removal of the explicit shared-representation limitation and tuning-selection details, and newly erroneous DARA classifier equations in Appendix C.1, limiting the overall quality gain.
